quests.instruction: Snap the scrambled words back into the order you hear.
quests.hint: 'There is' introduces something that exists — it isn't the real subject of the action.
quests.explanation: 'There is' announces that something exists (a queue), followed by where it is (at the counter). This differs from normal subject-first sentences.
quests.textToSpeak: There is a queue at the counter.

quests.instruction: Listen closely, then rebuild the sentence in the order you hear it.
quests.hint: The number word comes before the describing word, and both come before 'windows'.
quests.explanation: Subject (My room) + verb (has) + quantity + adjective + noun (two large windows). Number, then adjective, then noun — that order never changes.
quests.textToSpeak: My room has two large windows.

quests.instruction: Put the scrambled words back in the order you hear them.
quests.hint: 'Something' stands in for a person or thing we can't name exactly — it starts the sentence like any subject would.
quests.explanation: 'Something' acts as the subject here, just like a noun would. 'With my order' explains what the problem relates to.
quests.textToSpeak: Something is wrong with my order.

quests.instruction: Snap the scrambled words back into the order you hear.
quests.hint: 'Some' attaches to the object, not the subject — listen for what follows it.
quests.explanation: Subject (I) + verb (bought) + quantifier + noun (some vegetables) + place (at the market). 'Some' is used for an unspecified amount.
quests.textToSpeak: I bought some vegetables at the market.

quests.instruction: Listen closely, then rebuild the sentence in the order you hear it.
quests.hint: 'Many' pairs with countable plural nouns like 'friends'.
quests.explanation: Subject (We) + verb (have) + quantifier + noun (many friends) + place (in this city). 'Many' emphasizes a large number.
quests.textToSpeak: We have many friends in this city.

quests.instruction: Put the scrambled words back in the order you hear them.
quests.hint: Three small words build up the object one piece at a time: quantity, then opinion, then the noun.
quests.explanation: 'A few' (small quantity) + 'interesting' (opinion) + 'books' (noun) stack together before the noun in that fixed order.
quests.textToSpeak: She owns a few interesting books.

quests.instruction: Snap the scrambled words back into the order you hear.
quests.hint: 'But' signals a contrast — the second idea cancels part of the first.
quests.explanation: 'He likes tea' (positive) + 'but not coffee' (contrast) shows a preference between two similar things using 'but'.
quests.textToSpeak: He likes tea but not coffee.

quests.instruction: Listen closely, then rebuild the sentence in the order you hear it.
quests.hint: Two opposite-feeling adjectives are joined by 'but' — length first, then feeling.
quests.explanation: Subject (The movie) + verb (was) + adjective 1 (short) + 'but' + adjective 2 (exciting). 'But' links two adjectives that seem to disagree.
quests.textToSpeak: The movie was short but exciting.

quests.instruction: Put the scrambled words back in the order you hear them.
quests.hint: There's a short pause exactly where 'but' begins the second half — listen for that break.
quests.explanation: Clause 1 (I want to help) + 'but' + clause 2 (I have no time). Each half of a 'but' sentence could stand alone as its own sentence.
quests.textToSpeak: I want to help, but I have no time.

quests.instruction: Snap the scrambled words back into the order you hear.
quests.hint: 'Because' introduces the reason — it comes after the result, not before it.
quests.explanation: Result (She stayed home) + 'because' + reason (she felt sick). In spoken English, the result usually comes first, then the explanation.
quests.textToSpeak: She stayed home because she felt sick.

quests.instruction: Listen closely, then rebuild the sentence in the order you hear it.
quests.hint: The weather explanation sits in the second half, right after 'because'.
quests.explanation: Result (We took a taxi) + 'because' + reason (it was raining). 'It' refers to the weather, not a specific object.
quests.textToSpeak: We took a taxi because it was raining.

quests.instruction: Put the scrambled words back in the order you hear them.
quests.hint: Notice the tense shift: the first verb is past, but the reason uses present.
quests.explanation: Result (He saved money, past) + 'because' + reason (he wants a bike, present). Reasons can stay in present tense even when the main action is past.
quests.textToSpeak: He saved money because he wants a bike.

quests.instruction: Snap the scrambled words back into the order you hear.
quests.hint: Size comes before color — 'big' arrives before 'blue'.
quests.explanation: Subject (I) + verb (bought) + size + color + noun (a big blue suitcase). English usually orders adjectives as size, then color, then noun.
quests.textToSpeak: I bought a big blue suitcase.

quests.instruction: Listen closely, then rebuild the sentence in the order you hear it.
quests.hint: Size again leads, followed by a feeling-word, before the noun itself.
quests.explanation: Subject (They) + verb (rent) + size + feeling + noun (a small cozy apartment). 'Cozy' describes comfort, placed closest to the noun.
quests.textToSpeak: They rent a small cozy apartment.

quests.instruction: Put the scrambled words back in the order you hear them.
quests.hint: Length comes first this time, then the color, then the item.
quests.explanation: Subject (She) + verb (wore) + length + color + noun (a long red scarf). The same size-before-color pattern applies to length too.
quests.textToSpeak: She wore a long red scarf.

quests.instruction: Snap the scrambled words back into the order you hear.
quests.hint: 'First' opens the sentence; a matching 'then' opens the second half.
quests.explanation: 'First' + action 1 (I shower) + 'then' + action 2 (I get dressed). This pattern shows two steps happening in a fixed order.
quests.textToSpeak: First I shower, then I get dressed.

quests.instruction: Listen closely, then rebuild the sentence in the order you hear it.
quests.hint: Same pattern as before, but listen closely — the actions are shorter this time.
quests.explanation: 'First' + action 1 (we order) + 'then' + action 2 (we pay). Even short two-word clauses can follow this sequencing pattern.
quests.textToSpeak: First we order, then we pay.

quests.instruction: Put the scrambled words back in the order you hear them.
quests.hint: This time 'first' moves to the middle of the sentence instead of the very start.
quests.explanation: Action 1 (He studies) + 'first' + 'then' + action 2 (he relaxes). 'First' can follow the verb instead of opening the sentence — both positions are natural.
quests.textToSpeak: He studies first, then he relaxes.

quests.instruction: Snap the scrambled words back into the order you hear.
quests.hint: 'Their' matches 'neighbors' — both are plural, and they stay linked in meaning.
quests.explanation: Subject (My neighbors) + verb (park) + object (their cars) + place (outside). 'Their' agrees with the plural subject even though it appears later.
quests.textToSpeak: My neighbors park their cars outside.

quests.instruction: Listen closely, then rebuild the sentence in the order you hear it.
quests.hint: 'Their' again refers back to the subject, and 'tonight' closes the sentence.
quests.explanation: Subject (Our classmates) + verb (finish) + object (their projects) + time (tonight). The possessive 'their' must match the plural subject.
quests.textToSpeak: Our classmates finish their projects tonight.

quests.instruction: Put the scrambled words back in the order you hear them.
quests.hint: The manner word 'carefully' comes last, describing how the action is done.
quests.explanation: Subject (The workers) + verb (clean) + object (their tools) + manner (carefully). Manner adverbs typically follow the object at the end.
quests.textToSpeak: The workers clean their tools carefully.

quests.instruction: Snap the scrambled words back into the order you hear.
quests.hint: 'Too' means more than wanted — it comes right before the adjective it strengthens.
quests.explanation: Subject (This soup) + verb (is) + 'too' + adjective (spicy) + 'for me'. 'Too' shows an excessive amount, unlike 'very' which is neutral.
quests.textToSpeak: This soup is too spicy for me.

quests.instruction: Listen closely, then rebuild the sentence in the order you hear it.
quests.hint: 'Very' simply strengthens the adjective, without any negative meaning like 'too' has.
quests.explanation: Subject (The lecture) + verb (was) + 'very' + adjective (long) + time (today). 'Very' intensifies without judging whether it's good or bad.
quests.textToSpeak: The lecture was very long today.

quests.instruction: Put the scrambled words back in the order you hear them.
quests.hint: 'So' builds up the feeling word, and the reason phrase trails after it.
quests.explanation: Subject (She) + verb (felt) + 'so' + adjective (tired) + time (after work). 'So' often leads into an explanation, even when none follows here.
quests.textToSpeak: She felt so tired after work.

quests.instruction: Snap the scrambled words back into the order you hear.
quests.hint: The negative word splits the subject from the verb — listen for it right after 'I'.
quests.explanation: Subject (I) + 'don't' (negative auxiliary) + verb (like) + object (loud music). 'Don't' is the contraction of 'do not', used before the base verb.
quests.textToSpeak: I don't like loud music.

quests.instruction: Listen closely, then rebuild the sentence in the order you hear it.
quests.hint: With 'he', the negative word changes form, and the frequency word waits until the end.
quests.explanation: Subject (He) + 'doesn't' + verb (drink) + object (soda) + frequency (often). Third-person singular subjects need 'doesn't', not 'don't'.
quests.textToSpeak: He doesn't drink soda often.

quests.instruction: Put the scrambled words back in the order you hear them.
quests.hint: 'Anymore' signals a change from the past — it always sits at the very end of a negative sentence.
quests.explanation: Subject (They) + 'don't' + verb (live) + place (here) + 'anymore'. 'Anymore' means 'not now, although it used to be true'.
quests.textToSpeak: They don't live here anymore.

quests.instruction: Snap the scrambled words back into the order you hear.
quests.hint: An adjective sits inside the subject group, and two time words close the sentence together.
quests.explanation: Subject (The new manager) + verb (starts) + time (on Monday morning). 'On' pairs with named days, even when a part of the day follows.
quests.textToSpeak: The new manager starts on Monday morning.

quests.instruction: Listen closely, then rebuild the sentence in the order you hear it.
quests.hint: Two different actions with two different objects are joined by 'and' — listen for where the second object starts.
quests.explanation: Subject (We) + verb 1 + object 1 (ordered coffee) + 'and' + verb 2 + object 2 (shared a sandwich). Each verb keeps its own object.
quests.textToSpeak: We ordered coffee and shared a sandwich.

quests.instruction: Put the scrambled words back in the order you hear them.
quests.hint: This sentence stacks two time ideas at the end — listen for both and their order.
quests.explanation: Subject (My neighbor) + verb (waters) + object (his garden) + frequency (every evening) + time (after work). Longer time chains still follow logical order, general to specific.
quests.textToSpeak: My neighbor waters his garden every evening after work.
